requirements.text: Regarding the workstation with serial 'DESKTOP-NYC-145', we need to transition it to 'in_use' status
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_002' AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: DESKTOP-NYC-145 resolves to CI_002 (Aisha Desktop), the only CI with that serial; no other serial nearly matches
weak: CI_002 is already in_use on the seed, so the transition changes nothing; kept because the request asks it and the final state must still show it
no benchmark check tests the status

requirements.text: The new custodian is Sarah Connor, a new agent joining the Service Desk team in New York—generate a profile for her (sarah.connor@example.com, +1-555-010-9999)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE user_id = 'USER_011' AND user_name = 'sarah.connor' AND first_name = 'Sarah' AND last_name = 'Connor' AND email = 'sarah.connor@example.com' AND phone = '+1-555-010-9999' AND role = 'agent' AND active = 1 AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND location_id = 'LOC_001'
requirements.source: Checking for creation of new user.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (USER_011 after USER_010); the only user the task creates
user_name 'sarah.connor' kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the seed's convention is first.last)
active = 1 kept from the benchmark check; a new joiner who will own an asset must be active (policy 8.1)
location_id LOC_001: 'in New York' resolves to TechCorp NYC Headquarters, the only New York location on the seed
org_id ORG_001 (TechCorp): the New York location, the Service Desk Operations group and the acting user all belong to it; first_name, last_name and org_id are not in the benchmark check
a user_role row is not required: the request fixes nothing about it and no listed tool names that table

requirements.text: map her to the 'Service Desk Operations' group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 'MEMBER_006' AND group_id = 'GROUP_002' AND user_id = 'USER_011'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (MEMBER_006 after MEMBER_005); the only membership the task creates
'Service Desk Operations' resolves to GROUP_002 (exact name match, one row, ORG_001)
user_id USER_011, the profile created by the previous requirement

requirements.text: formally assign the asset to her
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_002' AND owner_id = 'USER_011' AND name = 'Aisha Desktop'
assumptions: the asset is CI_002 (serial DESKTOP-NYC-145); its previous owner USER_004 Aisha Williams gets the closing notification
owner_id USER_011, the profile created above
name 'Aisha Desktop' kept from the benchmark check (its selector); the request never asks to rename the CI, so a rename fails this as it fails the benchmark

disagreement: name cell: A omits it, B 'Aisha Desktop'; chose B because the benchmark check selects by that name and nothing in the request or policy contradicts it (the benchmark's check is the prior)

requirements.text: log a ticket for 'Setup Peripherals for Sarah Connor' with her as the caller
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND short_description = 'Setup Peripherals for Sarah Connor' AND caller_id = 'USER_011' AND status = 'new'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023); the only incident the task creates
status new from policy 3.1 (all new incidents are status = new); nothing in the request moves it
impact, urgency, priority, category and channel not cells: the request fixes none of them
incident.configuration_item not a cell: the hardware is attached through incident_affected_cis (next requirement), as the benchmark check and the listed tool do

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_affected_cis_id = 'TASKCI_004' AND configuration_item = 'CI_002' AND incident_id = 'INC_024'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (TASKCI_004 after TASKCI_003); the only affected-CI link the task creates
'the hardware' is CI_002, the workstation named at the start of the request; it is in_use, so policy 5.1 allows the link
INC_024 is the setup ticket's id, assumed next in sequence

requirements.text: ensuring ... the 'Desktop Boot Failure Troubleshooting' article [is] attached
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_003' AND used_as IN ('suggested', 'applied', 'resolution')
assumptions: 'Desktop Boot Failure Troubleshooting' resolves to KB_003 (exact title match, one row, published)

selected by incident and article, not by id: policy 7 has the agent link every matching article as suggested when the incident is created, so this link's sequence position is not fixed; the benchmark check selects the same way
used_as not stated; policy 7 requires one of suggested, applied, resolution (the column is NOT NULL), and the request attaches the article explicitly, so suggested and applied are both defensible

disagreement: row selection: A a selector on incident_id and knowledge_id, B an anchor on IKB_006; chose the selector because policy 7's search rule can add other links to INC_024, so the task may create more than one row in this table

disagreement: used_as cell: A IN ('suggested', 'applied', 'resolution'), B untested; chose A because policy 7 fixes the allowed set and the predicate is tighter without excluding any reading of the request

requirements.text: Conclude by notifying that previous owner we found earlier that 'Sarah's account, asset, and setup ticket have been successfully processed.'

cells.message: LIKE '%Sarah''s account, asset, and setup ticket have been successfully processed%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND email = 'aisha.williams@techcorp.com' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND message LIKE '%Sarah''s account, asset, and setup ticket have been successfully processed%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
the previous owner is Aisha Williams (USER_004, aisha.williams@techcorp.com), CI_002's owner on the seed
message tested by containment, as the benchmark check does; subject, type and status not fixed by request or policy

disagreement: incident_id cell: A omits it (not stated), B INC_024; chose B because notification.incident_id is NOT NULL in the schema, the message names the setup ticket, and INC_024 is the only incident the task creates or touches

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the eight requirements (the same tables, rows and sources, including the weak in_use transition as the one new requirement) and on all seven dispositions (kept); four cells differ. disagreement: name cell on the owner change: A omits it, B 'Aisha Desktop'; kept because the benchmark check selects by that name and the request never asks to rename the CI (logged in requirement 4). disagreement: row selection for the knowledge link: A a selector on incident_id and knowledge_id, B an anchor on IKB_006; chose the selector because policy 7's search rule can add other links to the new incident, so the row's sequence position is not fixed, and the benchmark check selects the same way (logged in requirement 7). disagreement: used_as on the knowledge link: A IN ('suggested', 'applied', 'resolution'), B untested; chose A because policy 7 fixes that set and the column is NOT NULL (logged in requirement 7). disagreement: incident_id on the notification: A omits it, B INC_024; chose B because the column is NOT NULL, the message names the setup ticket, and INC_024 is the only incident the task creates or touches (logged in requirement 8). Seed facts re-checked at merge: CI_002 is DESKTOP-NYC-145 (in_use, owner USER_004 Aisha Williams, aisha.williams@techcorp.com, LOC_001, ORG_001); GROUP_002 is Service Desk Operations (ORG_001); KB_003 is Desktop Boot Failure Troubleshooting (published); LOC_001 is the only New York location; USER_010, MEMBER_005, INC_023, TASKCI_003, IKB_005 and NOTIF_007 are the highest ids; no near matches to the serial, group name or article title, so no boundary stay is needed. Anchors assume the agent creates exactly one row per table in sequence, except the knowledge link. Policy 7's search rule names no articles, so no requirement is written for other suggested links. org_id is tested only on the new user; on the link rows, the incident and the notification it is ORG_001 by every route but left untested.
